request.voice_description: An original older male Western river guide. Very thick American frontier drawl, low mid register, dry leathery gravel, slow stretched vowels, warm but weather worn and practical. Natural conversational storytelling, clearly intelligible, not an announcer. Clean studio audio, no music, no effects. No imitation of a known person.
request.text: Easy there, partner. The river takes its own sweet time, and so do I. Pull your hat down, check the ropes, and keep your eyes on the far bank. We have a good long trail ahead of us.

request.text: Now hold on a minute, friend. I never said I had all the answers. You ask your questions mighty fast, and a fellow needs a moment to think. There is no cause for all this fuss, is there?

request.voice_description: A completely original male Western sheriff about fifty. Distinctive coppery medium-low baritone, dry creaky phrase endings, measured American frontier drawl and sharply articulated consonants. Calm local authority, patient, firm, with a wry warmth. Clearly different from a nasal prisoner and a slow gravelly river guide. Natural close speech, no announcer performance. Clean studio audio, no music or effects; no imitation of any existing actor or character.
request.text: All right, gentlemen. We settle things fair in this town. Keep your hands where I can see them, stand easy, and listen close. Nobody moves before the bell. You have my word on that.
